verified_relative_terrain_collapse.status: The following geometric implication has a complete coordinate-level homotopy and cover verification. Its hypothesis that the tube has been put in the terrain-cap form is not yet established for the actual normal tube.
verified_relative_terrain_collapse.hypotheses: Work in a large closed ball B_R about a point of plane z=0. Let F_1,...,F_c be disjoint closed planar disks strictly inside its equatorial disk. Let h be continuous on that disk, h=0 outside the interiors of the F_i, h<0 inside each F_i, and h above the lower hemisphere. Suppose the truncated exterior decomposes as X=A union B, with A=X intersection {z>=0}, B={(q,z): -sqrt(R²-|q|²)<=z<=h(q)}, and A intersection B={(q,0):q notin union int(F_i)}. Thus the cap interior D_i={(q,h(q)):q in int(F_i)} is disjoint from A, with boundary circle contained in A.
verified_relative_terrain_collapse.homotopy: On A use the identity. On B define H_s(q,z)=(q,(1-s)z+s h(q)), 0<=s<=1. The segment stays in each lower vertical interval and hence in B. On A intersection B, z=h(q)=0 so this is the identity. A and B are closed in the compact X, so the closed-pasting lemma makes H jointly continuous. At s=1 it maps X onto Y=A union graph(h); Y is fixed at every time. Therefore H is a strong deformation retraction.
verified_relative_terrain_collapse.annular_open_cover: Choose supplied disk charts phi_i:closed unit disk→graph(h|F_i). Fix 0<r0<r1<1. Set V_i=phi_i({r<r1}) and U=Y minus union_i phi_i({r<=r0}). Each omitted inner disk is closed in Y, so U is relative-open. Each V_i is relative-open because its closure stays away from A and from the other cap disks, and on the cap interior Y has precisely the ordinary disk topology. Their union covers Y since r0<r1. V_i is contractible, V_i intersection V_j empty, and U intersection V_i=phi_i({r0<r<r1}), an open annulus. The map r↦(1-s)r+s on the cap collars, identity on A, gives a deformation retraction U→A; continuity follows at r=1 since phi_i(1,theta) lies in A and is fixed. Consequently any proved meridian-wedge SDR of A supplies the required U basis.
verified_relative_terrain_collapse.infinity: Choose R beyond the whole tube. Outside B_R the explicit radial homotopy q↦((1-s)+s R/|q|)q retracts to the enclosing sphere and fixes the sphere. It never touches the tube. Glue with identity inside B_R, then perform the terrain homotopy. The sphere at infinity is retained in the truncated exterior and mapped to Y; it is not discarded or filled. In particular all c cap disks remain, unlike a compact S3 exterior model with only c-1 essential 2-handles.
verified_relative_terrain_collapse.boundary_neighborhoods: The cover above lives on Y itself and needs no guessed open cover of the ambient 3-manifold. Its overlaps are actual annuli, not merely spaces with cyclic fundamental group. Ordered attachments and disjointness follow immediately from the explicit radii.

verified_two_handle_relative_collapse.status: Complete explicit auxiliary local model, independent of knot normal-form realization.
verified_two_handle_relative_collapse.formula: For t>=0 put q+=(0,2), lambda=min(1/|x|,2/(2-t)), interpreting 1/0 as +infinity. The endpoint is P=q+ + lambda((x,t)-q+). For s in [0,1], H_s=q+ + (1-s+s lambda)((x,t)-q+). For t<=0 use q-=(0,-2), lambda=min(1/|x|,2/(2+t)) and the same ray formula.
verified_two_handle_relative_collapse.verification: The first ray intersection beyond (x,t) is either the side |x|=1 or the middle t=0; before that point the ray stays in its half-cylinder. On side or middle lambda=1, so the whole target is fixed. At t=0 both formulas give lambda=1 and fix every x, hence they agree. The minima are continuous including x=0 since the finite t term dominates near x=0. The formulas therefore define an SDR, relative to the entire attaching side annulus. Products/collars can be collapsed without moving existing attachments.

upper_meridian_region_design.status: Topology and proposed finite normalization identified; full relative chart realization still to be written.
upper_meridian_region_design.geometry: After deleting a small underpass neighborhood at each crossing, projected upper arcs are embedded and pairwise disjoint, including no interior self-crossings: every underpassing point was removed. Place the surviving arcs at a common high level, with endpoint legs to z=0. Vertical curtains beneath their disjoint planar projections give supplied pairwise disjoint boundary-parallelism disks. The upper half-ball minus a neighborhood of these boundary-parallel arcs is a genus-c handlebody. To use this as a local proof, give the finite rectangular chart identifications that cutting along each curtain produces a ball, and collapse the resulting 0-handle/1-handle blocks to a graph.
upper_meridian_region_design.basing_paths: A basepoint above every arc can be connected through a fixed upper horizontal collar to each arc chart, using one finite planar tree avoiding all projected arc strips at the high level. Meridians cross their own curtain once and no other curtain; after cutting the curtains, their access paths lie in the remaining ball. This verifies the specified free basis once the ball/handlebody chart decomposition is proved. Arbitrary uncoordinated basing paths cannot be substituted: Friedl p70 explicitly warns they may yield only normal generators.
upper_meridian_region_design.remaining_realization_gap: Construct an actual finite rectangular tunnel neighborhood N_rect of the normalized knot, with each lower U-shaped segment contained in a 3-ball cap whose bottom is a terrain graph and whose top face lies in z=0, punctured by its two upward tube exits. Show this is a regular product tube around that U-shaped segment, explicitly glue the upper product tubes, and identify the resulting pair (R³,N_rect) with the initially chosen sufficiently small normal tube pair through endpoint-compatible local isotopies. A sketch that the neighborhood is regular is insufficient. The relative terrain homotopy above and the cover verification need no further guessing once this gap is filled.
upper_meridian_region_design.no_false_acceptance: The actual c>0 item Statement is still not accepted. These formulas complete the collapse/pasting/open-annulus portions conditional on one clearly identified finite model realization; they do not assert that realization has already been proved.

Therefore the proposed longitude w a^{-3}=z a^{-6}. The proposed +1 surgery relation w a^{-2}=1 is z a^{-5}=1, the usual positive-trefoil Poincare-sphere relation once the peripheral geometry is established.
